And topical CBD hasn't been well-studied. There was a short 12-week trial done, where they used a CBD skin gel, and it didn't do any better than placebo. The gel got CBD into the blood at about the levels of the starting oral dose, 5 to 10mg/kg. The approved oral doses go up to 20 or 25mg/kg a day, so the dosing may have been too low. And CBD through the skin goes straight into the blood, while swallowed CBD passes through the liver first. The liver is where some of it gets converted to 7-OH-CBD, which stopped seizures in mice about as well as CBD itself, so the gel may have missed out on that too.

Some people get a warning before a seizure takes hold, which is called an aura. That's when the things people report can still stop it, depending on what sets their seizures off. If it's flashing or flickering light, cover one eye with a hand and turn away from the light, because closing the eyes doesn't block enough of it. Some people stop a seizure at the warning stage with a strong smell like jasmine, and some train themselves to link one smell with feeling calm and then sniff it when a seizure threatens. When overstimulation is what sets it off, a cool, quiet, dark and comfortable space can help.

Cannabis at the start of an aura can go either way, so it's for someone who already knows how it affects their seizures. Some people say smoking or vaping it the moment an aura starts keeps the seizure from going further, and one woman's EEG showed fewer seizure discharges on the days she smoked. Others say THC vapes and concentrates brought their seizures on. And in rats, high-THC smoke made absence seizures worse, which are the brief staring kind. Smoking or vaping also takes someone fully awake, so never try it on someone who's already convulsing.

Anything that could let someone hurt themselves in the next five minutes takes priority, so get the car keys out of reach and turn the stove off, and move them away from roads and balconies, or pools of water for that matter. Put any weapons away and keep the person away from crowds and strangers. If they want to post their big revelation about the universe, or message an ex, take the phone.

Letting them move around is fine, and pacing can help them burn off some of the fear. Just keep them from taking more of anything, since that only makes it stronger and longer. If they want to go confront somebody, that can wait until it's worn off. And if they want to leave, someone goes with them, in case they get lost or end up somewhere dangerous.
